subject: How LLMs Work — Karpathy
source_contract: Scope: every chapter in Karpathy’s February 5, 2025 video. Primary content: the video and its timestamped English captions, retrieved directly from YouTube and through vidIQ. No separate syllabus was supplied. Editorial dependency order is distinguished from source claims.

chapters.title: The token prediction engine
chapters.goal: Follow the path from internet text to a model that can generate new text. Data, tokens, weights, and context are different parts of this mechanism.

items.title: The map: training builds the engine; inference runs it
Data selection determines what the model gets to learn from
Tokens are the model’s units of text
Training changes weights to improve next-token predictions
Inference repeatedly selects and appends a token

chapters.title: From base model to assistant
chapters.goal: Use the prediction engine to explain why conversation formatting and supervised examples change the behavior of a base model.

items.title: The map: an assistant is a trained role
A base model continues a document
Conversation structure becomes a token sequence
Supervised fine-tuning teaches by example

chapters.title: Learning from outcomes
chapters.goal: Distinguish imitation from practice with feedback; then distinguish reliable outcomes from learned preference scores.

items.title: The map: imitation and outcome feedback teach differently
Reinforcement learning rewards successful attempts
Reasoning behavior can emerge under outcome training
AlphaGo shows why the scoring environment matters
RLHF optimizes a learned proxy for human preference

chapters.title: Why useful models still fail
chapters.goal: Derive practical limitations from representation, available context, training examples, and computation. These lessons depend on the training map.

items.title: The map: diagnose the source of a failure
Grounding puts the source into the current context
A model’s self-description is generated output
Intermediate tokens can carry intermediate computation
Easy for a person can be awkward for token prediction

chapters.title: Beyond a single text response
chapters.goal: Place multimodality, agents, and model access around the same core engine. Keep the lecture’s February 2025 forecasts separate from current facts.

items.title: The map: new media still need a representation
Long-running agents expose the problem of state
Separate the model from where you run it
